answer: A farm running 132 keys therefore forfeits that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation cheap. Because the haven stake is held until the willow settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the horizon audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 22% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a cheap one. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
